slides.texte_overlay:
How to be more interesting
than your phone
Ask questions that make people think. "What's something you changed your mind about this year?" Nobody reaches for their phone during a question like that.
Tell stories with a twist. Start with the strange part: "I got locked in a museum once." Curiosity beats any notification. Your attention is contagious.
Put your own phone away first. Face down isn't enough, put it in your pocket. People mirror you, and they'll give you their attention back.
React with real energy. Laugh, be surprised, ask "no way, then what?" People love talking to someone who's genuinely into the conversation.
Before: people drifted to their phones when I talked. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I always have a good story.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: people drifted to their phones when I talked. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I always have a good story.

slides.texte_overlay: Suggest something to do. A walk, a game, a new place to eat. Doing something together is always more fun than scrolling side by side.
Keep it light and short. Don't lecture. Say the interesting part, then pass the conversation back. Good talkers make others want to talk too.
